papers.title: Homogeneous polynomial approximation on symmetric convex bodies: A proof of Kro\'o's conjecture
papers.abstract: We resolve Kro\'o's 2004 conjecture on homogeneous polynomial approximation in every dimension, without smoothness or curvature assumptions. For every origin-symmetric convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ with nonempty interior, every continuous real function on $\partial K$ is uniformly approximated by sums of homogeneous polynomials of degrees $n$ and $n+1$ as $n\to\infty$. Moreover, approximation of the constant function by homogeneous polynomials of degree $2n$ is uniform over all such bodies in each fixed dimension. Via homogenization, we also resolve Kro\'o's 2019 weighted approximation conjecture for every convex admissible weight on Euclidean space. The key construction produces homogeneous polynomials with a common Gaussian boundary profile and localization errors controlled by arbitrary polynomial weights. Its analytic core is a weighted Gaussian approximation theorem: for \(d\ge2\), sufficiently broad Gaussians on $\mathbb R^{d-1}$ can be approximated by $e^{-f}F$, where $f$ is nonnegative, convex and Lipschitz with $f(0)=0$, and $F$ is a Schwartz function with Fourier support in an arbitrarily small ball about the origin. Small Fourier support allows Taylor truncation to a lower degree, while the remainder enforces decay through homogenization. We then use positive spherical quadrature and degree raising to yield the full approximation theorem.

papers.title: Data-driven Regularization for Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: In many applications, we are interested in studying an object of interest $x$. However, its properties are often not directly measurable. Instead, we only observe $y = F(x)$, where the (known) function $F$ is referred to as the forward mapping. To infer about $x$ from the observation $y$, we seek an (approximate) inverse mapping $x \approx F^{-1}(y)$. This process is known as solving the inverse problem. In practice, the inverse mapping $F^{-1}$ may be ill-defined or discontinuous, which forces us to choose a certain solution from many possible ones based on prior assumptions on $x$. Such assumptions about $x$ are typically incorporated into the inversion process through regularization. Therefore, the first part of this course focuses on the classical regularization theory of inverse problems. In the second part, we transition to algorithmic approaches for solving inverse problems. The foundation for this lies in the variational formulation of inverse problems, where reconstructions are obtained by minimizing specific functionals. Here, we will explore key optimization principles, discuss their practical implementation, and examine how they contribute to robust reconstructions. Today, classical methods are often modified to incorporate data-driven machine learning techniques, which improve the empirical performance. However, this often comes at the cost of explainability or convergence guarantees. Such properties are critical, for example, in medical applications, where one wants to be confident that reconstructed abnormalities are of physical nature and not phantoms resulting from the method. For these reasons, we discuss a number of machine learning methods for inverse problems, such as unrolling techniques, learned regularizers and plug-and-play methods, and explore their performance guarantees.

papers.title: Convergence of Levenberg--Marquardt method in Banach spaces
papers.abstract: We study the Levenberg--Marquardt method for nonlinear inverse problems in Banach spaces under a H\"{o}lder stability estimate. Under suitable assumptions on the geometry of the Banach space and the Fr\'{e}chet derivative of the measurement operator, we establish the well-definedness of the method, local convergence and convergence rates for exact data, and the monotonic decrease of the Bregman distance up to the stopping index for noisy data. These results extend the corresponding Hilbert space theory to the Banach space setting.

papers.title: Distributionally robust approximation property of neural networks
papers.abstract: The universal approximation property uniformly with respect to weakly compact families of measures is established for several classes of neural networks. To that end, we prove that these neural networks are dense in Orlicz spaces, thereby extending classical universal approximation theorems even beyond the traditional $L^p$-setting. The covered classes of neural networks include widely used architectures like feedforward neural networks with non-polynomial activation functions, deep narrow networks with ReLU activation functions and functional input neural networks.

papers.title: Stability of a Fr\'{e}chet-type functional equation
papers.abstract: We establish the generalized Hyers-Ulam stability of the Fr\'{e}chet-type functional equation \begin{align*} \sum_{\emptyset \neq I \subset \{ 1, 2, \ldots, n+1 \}} (-1)^{|I|-n+1} f \Bigg( \sum_{i \in I} x_i \Bigg) = 0 \end{align*} in the sense of G\u{a}vru\c{t}a.

papers.title: Logarithmic fractional Hardy inequalities
papers.abstract: We establish sharp fractional Hardy inequalities in the critical regimes $sp=d$ and $sp=1$, with explicit logarithmic weight functions. In the whole-space setting, for $p>d\ge 1$, $sp=d$, we prove that \begin{equation*} \int_{\mathbb R^d} \int_{\mathbb R^d} \frac{|u(x)-u(y)|^p}{|x-y|^{2d}}\,dx\,dy \geq \left(\frac{p-1}{p}\right)^p \int_{B_R}|u(x)|^p W_{p,d,R}(x)\,dx, \end{equation*} for $u\in C_c(B_R)$, where $W_{p,d,R}$ is a logarithmic-type weight and the constant is sharp. We also show that the corresponding inequality with the simpler weight $|x|^{-d}(\log(R/|x|))^{-p}$ cannot hold with any positive constant. Furthermore, we derive two-sided estimates and asymptotic formulae for $W_{p,d,R}$, including its limiting connection with the classical Hardy inequality. In the half-space $\mathbb{R}^{d}_{+}$, we establish an analogous sharp fractional Hardy inequality in the critical case $sp=1$, with an explicit logarithmic weight depending on the distance to the boundary. We also investigate the asymptotic behaviour of this weight, obtaining estimates that describe its behaviour near the boundary. These results elucidate the role of logarithmic weights in critical fractional Hardy inequalities in both whole-space and half-space settings.

papers.title: Electromagnetic Potentials via the Extended Maxwell System
papers.abstract: We construct electromagnetic potentials on arbitrary open 3-dimensional sets for anisotropic, non-homogeneous materials, thus rendering any topological assumption like simple connectedness or the absence of holes superfluous in this context. The main idea is to invoke the extended Maxwell system the easy solution theory of which then yields existence of both scalar- and vector potentials.

papers.title: Singularity removal in nonlocal operator inequalities on domains and applications
papers.abstract: We prove that certain classes of nonlocal integral estimates on domains, involving operators, may be reduced to the local analogues without the singular weight on cubes. The theory applies to two-sided inverse doubling and quasi-monotone kernels with some moment conditions, and with a left-hand-side operator with average domain-bi-Lipschitz properties. Direct applications to fractional semi-norm inequalities in Peridynamics, such as fractional Korn's inequalities and Geometric Rigidity Estimates are presented.

papers.title: Euler--Lagrange Flow Monotonicity for the Radon Transform
papers.abstract: We present a new gradient-like flow that targets critical points of the inequality for the planar Radon transform $\mathcal{R}$ proven by Oberlin and Stein, partially answering a question of Christ, who gave a complete characterisation of the extremisers of the inequality via rearrangement methods. We show that for non-negative radial initial data near the extremiser manifold, solutions to the flow exist globally and there exists a rescaled subsequence of the flow that converges to a critical point of the Radon functional $\|\mathcal{R} f\|_3/\|f\|_{3/2}$ locally in $L^{3/2}(\mathbb{R}^2)$. We also obtain a quantitative result for the rate of decay of critical points, which complements a result of Christ arXiv:1106.0719 in the special case of radial functions. We prove a novel localised smoothing estimate for the operator $\mathcal{R}^*[(\mathcal{R}\cdot)^2]$ restricted to radial functions. This approach is complementary to that of Christ and provides a robust framework for studying extremal problems associated to Radon-like operators.

papers.title: Notes on Orlicz Spaces and Interpolation
papers.abstract: Orlicz spaces are a natural generalization of classical Lebesgue spaces. They are built upon convex growth functions and provide a flexible framework for studying integrability conditions beyond power-type behavior. In this survey paper, we present the basic definitions, main properties, and fundamental results concerning Orlicz spaces, and also discuss the Marcinkiewicz interpolation result for Orlicz spaces.

papers.title: Finite-rank rigidity and Nash-curve discreteness for correlation potentials
papers.abstract: For every nonconstant real polynomial P of degree k and every positive rational exponent a/b, minimizing the spherical energy with potential |P(t)|^{a/b} admits a discrete solution with at most $\binom{d+2ak-1}{2ak}+\binom{d+2ak-2}{2ak-1}$ support points, where a/b is reduced. This finite-replacement consequence needs no denominator threshold. Under a multiplicity-sensitive denominator condition, we prove the stronger conclusion that every minimizer has an explicit uniform support bound; suitable negative positive-semidefinite perturbations preserve that bound. We present these consequences before the machinery. The main arguments simplify irrational-power finite-rank rigidity and give a Nash-curve ramification obstruction, stable under entire scalar additions, for powers, logarithms, and rational poles. The latter yields uniform finite supports on compact semialgebraic curves without assuming that the supports are semialgebraic. The known p-frame finite-replacement principle is distinguished from the extensions developed here. No unconditional discreteness theorem for general irrational p is claimed.

papers.title: Centro-Affine Differential Geometry and the Log-Minkowski Problem
papers.abstract: We interpret the log-Brunn-Minkowski conjecture of B\"or\"oczky-Lutwak-Yang-Zhang as a spectral problem in centro-affine differential geometry. In particular, we show that the Hilbert-Brunn-Minkowski operator coincides with the centro-affine Laplacian, thus obtaining a new avenue for tackling the conjecture using insights from affine differential geometry. As every strongly convex hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a centro-affine unit-sphere, it has constant centro-affine Ricci curvature equal to $n-2$, in stark contrast to the standard weighted Ricci curvature of the associated metric-measure space, which will in general be negative. In particular, we may use the classical argument of Lichnerowicz and a centro-affine Bochner formula to give a new proof of the Brunn-Minkowski inequality. For origin-symmetric convex bodies enjoying fairly generous curvature pinching bounds (improving with dimension), we are able to show global uniqueness in the $L^p$- and log-Minkowski problems, as well as the corresponding global $L^p$- and log-Minkowski conjectured inequalities. As a consequence, we resolve the isomorphic version of the log-Minkowski problem: for any origin-symmetric convex body $\bar K$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, there exists an origin-symmetric convex body $K$ with $\bar K \subset K \subset 8 \bar K$, so that $K$ satisfies the log-Minkowski conjectured inequality, and so that $K$ is uniquely determined by its cone-volume measure $V_K$. If $\bar K$ is not extremely far from a Euclidean ball to begin with, an analogous isometric result, where $8$ is replaced by $1+\epsilon$, is obtained as well.

papers.title: A class of port-Hamiltonian systems with general time delays
papers.abstract: We define a class of infinite dimensional linear port-Hamiltonian delay systems, give a characterization for such systems, and provide an easily verifiable sufficient condition to belong to this class, thereby extending the study by Breiten, Hinsen and Unger in [IEEE Trans. Autom. Control vol. 69, no. 12 (2024), pp. 8924-8930, doi: 10.1109/TAC.2024.3464332]. The results rely on the operator semigroup theoretic treatment of linear delay PDEs.

papers.title: Diffraction of rotated measures
papers.abstract: Consider a translation-bounded measure on the line. We can rotate the measure, distributing the mass proportionally to the area, to create a two-dimensional rotationally invariant translation-bounded measure. We show that the diffraction of the two-dimensional object is the normalised rotation of the diffraction of the original measure. We discuss some examples and generalisation beyond $d=2$.

papers.title: Local Hardy and bmo Spaces on Filtered Lie Groups
papers.abstract: We develop a theory of local Hardy and $bmo$ spaces on a connected Lie group with polynomial growth whose Lie algebra is endowed with a filtration. Under suitable assumptions, we prove that the local Hardy spaces enjoy an appropriate atomic decomposition, are compatible with Calder\'on--Zygmund operators, and can be identified with certain Triebel--Lizorkin spaces, as it happens in the classical settings.

papers.title: The equal norm Grassmannian: topology and applications to frame fields
papers.abstract: Given an orientable rank-$d$ vector bundle over a $d$-manifold, the Euler class is the unique obstruction to finding a nowhere-zero section. An equal norm Parseval frame is a certain collection of sections, one of whose properties is that the lengths of each vector at each point are equal. This makes the Euler class an obvious obstruction to finding such a frame. In this work we show that this is the only obstruction so long as the number of sections is at least $2d+2$. We also identify precise obstructions when the number of sections is $2d$ and produce examples showing that for smaller numbers of sections it is sometimes impossible to find Parseval frame fields.

papers.title: The convolution product is generally not an open map
papers.abstract: We show that the convolution product $\ell^1(G)\times \ell^1(G)\to \ell^1(G)$ is not an open map if $G$ is either non-abelian or contains an element of infinite order. The case $G=\mathbb Z$ solves a problem posed by Kania and Ma\'slany.

papers.title: Localization of generators of Markov processes via the Dynkin operator
papers.abstract: In this article, we consider a Feller process whose resolvent has the strong Feller property. Using the Dynkin operator of this process, we define local realizations of the generator on an open subset $U$ of its state space. In particular, this allows us to describe the generator of the process killed upon leaving a regular, open subset $U$ as a realization of a maximal operator subject to Dirichlet boundary conditions. Besides the definition via the Dynkin operator, we also consider other possible definitions of such a local realization: a definition in terms of the unkilled semigroup, a definition based on approximation with elements of the generator and a probabilistic definition using martingales. Under mild additional assumptions, we prove that all these definitions are equivalent.

papers.title: Selection spectra and sharp perturbations of normal sequences
papers.abstract: For a bounded sequence $y=(y_n)\subset E^*$ and $0<p<\infty$, let $$ G_p(y)=\{x\in E:(y_n(x))\in\ell_p\}, $$ and call $y$ $p$-strongly normal when $G_p(y)$ is dense in $E$. We study the spectra obtained by passing to subsequences and, for Schauder basic sequences, to normalized successive blocks. Their possible values are exactly $$ \varnothing,\quad (0,\infty),\quad (1,\infty),\quad [r,\infty),\quad (r,\infty)\qquad (r>1), $$ and the possible pairs are precisely the nested pairs. Every admissible pair has a normalized weakly null $1$-unconditional basic realization, even in the fixed dual $\ell_\infty(\mathfrak c)=\ell_1(\mathfrak c)^*$, and may be realized with empty spectrum for the original sequence. We also determine sharp universal perturbation classes: $\ell_p$ for $p$-strong normality at a fixed exponent, $c_0$ for the whole subsequence spectrum, and $\ell_1$ for the block spectrum. More generally, for every proper symmetric Banach sequence ideal $A\subsetneq c_0$, membership of the error sequence in $A$ is exactly the universal condition preserving density of the $A$-summability domain. Finally, we extend the author's 2012 selection example from exponent one to every $p>0$ and to every proper symmetric Banach sequence ideal. The good subsequences are exactly those whose index sets have uniformly bounded runs of consecutive integers; in the good case the detected quotient is isomorphic to $c_0$ and the whole selected sequence is weak-star Schauder basic.

papers.title: Characterization of sets in metric spaces where the big Lipschitz derivative is infinite
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a metric space without isolated points. In this paper we prove that $E$ is a $G_\delta$-set in $X$ if and only if there exists a continuous function $f:X\to\mathbb{R}$ whose big Lipschitz derivative is infinite precisely on $E$. To this end, we introduce a new generalization of the classical Takagi function to the setting of metric spaces.

papers.title: Exh subspaces of bounded variation spaces generated by submeasures
papers.abstract: In the present paper we are building one more bridge between the theory of ideals on the set of natural numbers and the theory of spaces of functions of bounded variation. It is already known that $F_\sigma$ ideals (that is, ideals of the form $\text{Fin}(\phi)$, where $\phi$ is a lower semicontinuous submeasure on $\mathbb{N}$) lead to a nice generalization of different concepts from the theory of functions of bounded variation (Waterman variation and Chanturya classes). In this paper we show that analytic P-ideals (that is, ideals of the form $\text{Exh}(\phi)$, where $\phi$ is a lower semicontinuous submeasure on $\mathbb{N}$) lead to a generalization of spaces of functions continuous in $\Lambda$-variation. The properties of this generalization are investigated.

papers.title: Uncertainty principles as forcing mechanisms
papers.abstract: In this note we first consider the Heisenberg uncertainty principle. We show that it acts as a {\bf forcing mechanism} in the following sense. Real functions that approach its limit are close to Gaussian distributions, with proximity both in the sense of total variation distance and Wasserstein-1 distance. We next consider the uncertainty principle for functions defined on finite Abelian groups, and show that it acts as a forcing mechanism in the following sense. Functions that approach its limit are close (after translation and modulation by a complex exponential) to indicator functions of some subgroup, with proximity measured in ${\mathbb {L}}^1$-norm.

papers.title: Coarse comparison of Bessel families
papers.abstract: We classify Bessel families in separable Hilbert spaces under coarse equivalence relations: $f$ and $\tilde f$ are equivalent if the seminorms $\|T_f\,\cdot\|$ and $\|T_{\tilde f}\,\cdot\|$ of their analysis operators are mutually dominated, up to constants, after pullback along operators $w,\tilde w$ of a prescribed class $\mathcal O$. In contrast with orbit relations such as unitary or similarity equivalence, these relations ignore redundancy and the geometry of the index set, and compare frames, nonframes and compact families on the same footing. They are level $-1$ of the comparison categories of the companion article, and we compute the levels $0$ and $k\ge1$: they are trivial for bounded, injective, bounded below, isometric and upper semi-Fredholm comparison operators, and for invertible or unitary ones level $1$ is a stabilizer-type group of the family. For bounded $\mathcal O$ the classes are given by the singular numbers up to constants; injective operators add the kernel dimension, bounded below operators or isometries add upper semi-Fredholmness, and invertible, unitary or surjective operators give the kernel dimension and the dyadic multiplicity sequence of the spectrum up to bounded displacement on the logarithmic scale, which splits each remaining class into continuum many. Upper semi-Fredholm operators give only three noncompact classes, whereas Fredholm operators give continuum many, so that the Fredholm relation is strictly finer. For each relation we determine exactly which families are equivalent to an orthonormal basis, and we compute an operator Banach--Mazur distance, $\log(\sup_ns_n/\tilde s_n\cdot\sup_n\tilde s_n/s_n)$. As applications, we obtain a relative Paley--Wiener stability theorem for Bessel families and the invariance of Schatten membership and of $\int\|f\|^2$ under coarse equivalence.

papers.title: Additive preservers of mutual strong numerical radius orthogonality
papers.abstract: Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space with $\dim H\ge2$. We show that the additive surjections on $\mathcal{B}(H)$ and on its self-adjoint part $\mathcal{B}_s(H)$ that preserve mutual strong numerical-radius orthogonality in one direction are precisely the maps of the form $A\mapsto cUAU^*$, where $U$ is a unitary or antiunitary operator on $H$ and $c$ is a nonzero complex or real scalar, respectively.

papers.title: Sharp derivative inequalities for maximal functions
papers.abstract: We determine the optimal constant in the $L^p$-derivative inequality for the uncentered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator on the real line for every $1<p<\infty$. It is the unique number $\gamma_p\in [0,1]$ satisfying $(2p-1)\gamma_p+(p-1)\gamma_p^{(2p-1)/(p-1)}=p$. As $p$ goes from $1$ to $+\infty$, $\gamma_p$ decreases from $1$ to $\sqrt2-1$, and at the endpoints the limiting arguments recover the classical total-variation and Lipschitz inequalities, with the qualitative regularity ingredient at the $BV$ endpoint supplied by Aldaz and P\'erez L\'azaro.

papers.title: On an affirmative solution to Michael's problem, with applications to automatic continuity theory
papers.abstract: In 1952, Michael posed a question about functional continuity of commutative Fr\'{e}chet algebras in his memoir, known as Michael's problem in the literature. We settle this in the affirmative along with its equivalent forms. Indeed, we continue our previous works to directly attack these problems. We show that the test case for this problem -- the Fr\'{e}chet algebra $\cal U$ of all entire functions on $\ell^\infty$ -- is, in fact, a Fr\'{e}chet algebra $\cc[[X]]$, if there exists a discontinuous character on $\cal U$. An important tool is a topological version of the tensor (symmetric) algebra over a Banach space. The elementary, but crucial, idea is to express the test algebra $\cal U$ as a {\it weighted Fr\'{e}chet symmetric algebra} over the Banach space $\ell^1$. We summarize the effects of our affirmative solution in terms of important applications in automatic continuity theory, including affirmative answers to two significant, long-standing problems from 1966 and 1978.

papers.title: The functional analytic approach establishes the Corona theorem in the theory of SCV
papers.abstract: We give an affirmative solution of the original Corona problem (1962) for certain bounded pseudoconvex domains or polydomains in $\mathbb{C}^n$, including the balls and polydiscs, by using the Gleason solvability property of such domains for $H^\infty(G)$. In fact, we establish an equivalency of the Corona problem and Gleason's problem (1964) in the theory of several complex variables. Indeed, we extend our recent works on both problems based on the functional analytic approaches, and extend recent work of Clos, as well as apply the usual Banach algebra method. As an application, we establish the I. J. Schark's theorem for these $G$'s. We also obtain a welcome extension of a result of Krantz and Li (1995) for a bounded, strictly pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb{C}^n$ with $C^3$ boundary.

papers.title: On certain mapping properties of a weighted totally geodesic $k$-plane transform on the real hyperbolic space
papers.abstract: In this article, we study a weighted analogue of the totally geodesic $k$-plane transform on the real hyperbolic space. Throughout the article, we are concerned with the mapping properties of this transform. Particularly, we first consider the existence of the operator on weighted Lebesgue spaces, where the weights under consideration are natural to the geometry of the hyperbolic space. Then, we proceed to see the $L^p$-improving mapping properties of the said transform on radial functions. Further, we also prove end-point boundedness results on Lorentz spaces of radial functions. Lastly, we look into the problem of weighted $L^p$-$L^p$ boundedness, and obtain partial results in this direction. In the way of obtaining these results, we also give a spherical integral representation of the weighted totally geodesic $k$-plane transform.

papers.title: Sharp Tilting Inequalities
papers.abstract: For positive semidefinite matrices $A,B$ and $1/2\le\alpha\le1$, we establish $\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[A\,D\log(A^\alpha+B^\alpha)(B^\alpha)\right] \le s^s(1-s)^{1-s}\operatorname{Tr}[A^\alpha B^{1-\alpha}]$, where $s=(1-\alpha)/\alpha$, with the optimal coefficient. The proof uses a superoperator representation of the directional derivative of the logarithm and an Araki-type estimate for the derivative of a fractional power. Both this inequality and its symmetric-quotient counterpart extend to positive trace-class $A$ and positive, possibly unbounded, self-adjoint $B$ on a separable Hilbert space.

papers.title: Riccati Equations and the Third Problem of Halmos
papers.abstract: Rencently, Fang, Hou, Jiang, and Zhang reduced Halmos's third problem to invertible operators with conjugate bi-geometric form. An operator has such a form if, with respect to an orthogonal decomposition, it admits a representation $$ T = \begin{pmatrix} A & C \\ 0 & B \end{pmatrix}, \quad A^*, B \in B_1(O_\delta),$$ where $O_\delta=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|<\delta\}$ for some $\delta>0$, and $B_1(O_\delta)$ denotes the rank-one Cowen--Douglas class. We restrict our attention to the case $B=A^*$ with strictly positive coupling $C$, and settle Halmos's third problem for this class of operators. More precisely,we prove that every such operator $T$ is invertible and that $T^{-1}$ has a nontrivial closed invariant subspace. This result contributes to the study of Halmos's third problem within the conjugate bi-geometric framework.The proof combines monotone solutions of operator Riccati equations with strong operator convergence to construct invariant subspaces for associated Hamiltonian operator matrices.
